answer.generated: To calculate the output size of a pooling layer, given an input image size of 10x10 and a pooling size (∆) of 3, we need to understand how the pooling operation reduces the dimensions of the input image. The pooling operation partitions the image into patches of size ∆x∆, and then applies a reduction operation on each patch. In this case, with ∆=3, each patch will be of size 3x3. After performing the reduction operation (either max-pooling or mean-pooling), the spatial dimensions of the image are reduced accordingly. Specifically, the formula for the output size after pooling is ⌊m/∆⌋×⌊n/∆⌋, where m and n are the dimensions of the input image, and ∆ is the pooling size. Applying this formula, the output size becomes ⌊10/3⌋×⌊10/3⌋, which simplifies to 3x3. Therefore, the output image size after passing through a pooling layer with a pooling size of 3 will be 3x3. This reduction in dimensionality helps in decreasing the computational complexity while retaining important features of the input image.
